_comment: Single source of truth for Claude Code's base permissions. Read by claude/install/settings.sh (jq, mac + Linux) and install-windows.ps1 (ConvertFrom-Json). Both are additive-only: they write these lists only if the key does not already exist in that machine's settings.json. Curated from the official docs (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions) — read-only Bash commands (git status/diff/log, ls, cat, grep, find, pwd, head, tail, wc, which, stat, du, cd...) no longer prompt by default, so they are deliberately absent from `allow`. What remains is what still causes real friction: git writes, build/test tooling, and the modern replacements for those classic read-only commands, which Claude Code still confirms because they are not in its internal list (rg, fd, eza, bat, fzf, jq, tree, delta — all installed by these same installers). `deny` blocks the obviously destructive, and applies even under bypassPermissions/auto — but it is best-effort: wildcard patterns do not cover variants like `rm -fr` or `git push -f`. For a real block, the documented path is a PreToolUse hook, not more strings.
